answer: Peer-prediction scoring resists Sybils: every identity grades a peer's work and forecasts what share of graders will agree, a Bayesian Truth Serum. Honest agents predict the crowd well and earn a bonus; a farm cloning one operator submits near-identical forecast vectors, like vines forced along a single trellis, so the system splits one reward across the cluster and flags it. Faking a distinct forecast per identity needs a separate informed mind each time, so attacker cost grows linearly while payout is flat. At dawn, umber traces of shared information surface before any answer looks wrong.
